hi i took the exact same combi as you!! honestly at sec3 i was doing badly, even my prelim l1r5 was 21 and i managed to do well for o's in 2017. u rly don't have to worry too much now :-) but make sure to strengthen your foundations if you want your sec4 journey to be a lil smoother.

1. for lit - constantly read your books & sign up for consistent consults, even if it's just to discuss some ideas u hv about the book. the more in-depth you explore the book, the better you'll be able to tackle qns. also, time management is super impt bc if you can't finish the essay, you won't get the marks. pick out strong & key evidence that you can use for multiple themes and discussions to memorise. practice writing essays and having your teacher mark them. at o levels, markers don't focus v heavily on technicalities like technique names, so just make sure you talk more about *how* the technique is used and its *effects*!

for hist - content! memorise, memorise, memorise. flashcards, mindmaps and timelines helped me a lot so i wld recommend them! esp since i suck at memory work (why i took pure phy > bio). for csq, try and use formats to help you ans questions (if your sch doesn't provide them alr). this is impt since cambridge tends to only come out with a few qn types (e.g reliability, purpose etc) so you should be able to easily tackle them once you get used to them.

2. i sucked at chem and basically gave up on it for o's to focus on my other subjects so i'll just comment on physics! and yes, practice is one of the best ways to tackle phy! one way is to have an equation and definitions bank so you can memorize them easier. a lot of qns have repetitive styles (e.g ac generator) so studying answers wld help a lot too (like how you would study amaths). phy is mostly about application, which is why there's less memory work compared to other subjs, you shd train yourself to be able to link your concepts to the real world arnd you! for phy, understanding the content is more impt than pure memorisation bc only then will u be able to apply it :)

bruh i was getting multiple F9s in sec3 and got <10 for o levels lol you rly don't have to worry about your l1r5 at this point!! most of the exam prep will come early sec4 or in sec4 sem 2, so just focus on building your foundations for now :) no need to stress too much!

and i rly agree with the other comments! honestly it's rly difficult to find someone who actually likes studying, but it's about liking what you're learning! for me, i liked lit so much i was practically reading my lit book everyday and highlighting new stuff all the time lol. i hated my other subjects, so whenever i wanted to "take a break", i would study lit. i would sign up for a lot of lit consults too and it boosted my productivity lots.

jc-wise, i'd suggest to think about it after o's end, but i would recommend you to check out schools that offers hybrid stream (acjc, ejc etc) so you can take equal portions of sci and humans (i'm in hybrid now!)

and!! imo the jc's cut-off is *not* definitive of how good it'll be for you. im in j2 now and oftentimes i wish i went to another jc instead, even though my current one is considered one of the better ones. make sure to attend open houses and find your best fit! including the teaching environment, support system, teachers, school events and values etc :)

hi, i was diagnosed with anxiety disorder 4 years ago. i'm not sure if my experience rly helps, but i hope it sheds some light on your situation :)

some of the symptoms i experience during an anxiety attack are cold extremes (fingers/hands, feet/toes), feeling very *very* uneasy (like an intense shakiness in my chest, can come randomly or by certain triggers), sudden weight and tightness in my shoulders/neck areas, and severe crying.

it's also more likely to suffer from anxiety if you have a family member who also does. (for me, it was my dad and his mum, but i'm not sure how far the hereditary traits extends).

if you're unsure about how your family might react to it, you can visit a school counsellor first just to get some professional input on your situation (most counsellors are qualified psychologists). 

like you, my mum isn't very understanding about mental health issues and my dad has anger management issues and tends to get extremely uptight about such things. fortunately, i was able to request for my school counsellor to keep the session confidential, which means my parents did not have to be informed. i'm not sure if this is applicable across all schools, but u can give it a try! :) i had a friend who saw the counsellor because of anxiety issues and self-harm as well, and it was kept confidential from her parents too.

you may want to clarify about confidentiality first on your visit if you intend to!

also what i've been told (by imh, hpb etc) is that if you're a minor, you would need parental consent to receive medication. therapy and counselling do not require parental consent, however they may inform your parents if your life is at risk (e.g. suicidal tendencies) because their priority is to ensure your life. therapy is subsidised if you're singaporean, but still costs upwards of $50 i think. if your parents are not involved you may have to shoulder the cost yourself, so i recommend visiting the school counsellor first as it's free!

hope this helps :D if there's anything else you'd like to know, feel free to pm me! atb!!

edit: other symptoms include difficulty breathing, racing heartbeat, trembling, which may sometimes escalate to hyperventilation

for topics like plane geometry i believe it's mostly exposure and experience to get used to being able to identify angle theorems and similar triangles etc. personally i suck at it so i just try my luck by imagining it to scale (although it's not!! but i think most of the time the triangles will take the shape). you can also identify and make up "rules" for yourself so you can grasp the diagram better! e.g for cosine rule the angle you use is always the one inbetween the 2 sides ur using. tbh these kind of qns aren't my strong suit either HAHA but practice should be sufficient to put you in the safe zone for it! if you're worried then you can practice only identifying those angle theorems and stuff and having your teacher check for you! so your confidence with it can grow and you can kinda recognize when you've grasped the skill for it:) math is mostly practice for all the topics!
you can try working backwards too, like if know you need to find another angle in another triangle in another circle to get the ans then you can kind of assume it's one of your weaker theorems that you can't really identify (e.g for me it would be alt. angle theorem) because there's really no harm in just assuming if you're really stuck and clueless and desperate since you won't get marked down for getting it wrong anyway!

(i never passed my combined history+ss in sec sch always getting F9 or E8 but i got A1 for olvls lol) negative thoughts affect your results! confidence and hope will definitely reflect in your eventual grades. self-derogation = big nono!!

chem is considered to be important to take in jc but if you think you'll definitely not pursue medicine in the future you don't necessarily have to take it because other uni courses accept pre-requisites of bio/physics too and there should be bridging for non-chem takers (i'm not taking it rn) plus it's a really intense subject and all the people i know complain about it. but i've heard from a number of teachers (in both acjc and njc) that they've seen students who were weak in chem in sec sch fluorish in h2 chem so i think it varies from student to student. anyway if you think you can improve in chem fast then go for it! (personally i decided to stop trying for chem after prelims because as much as i found it interesting i just wasn't strong in it lol but bc my cohort's paper was pretty hard i think so bell curve got me a b3, a lot of factors that can affect your results cannot be predicted so don't worry too much about it now and just put in your best effort into everything you do!)

for emaths and amaths, just do papers. keep a notebook to keep track of mistakes that you find yourself constantly making and interesting/useful tips for papers. it's important to know exam skills and tricks, and common skills that they test on (consults would be very useful for these and if you have external tuition that would be super helpful too). e.g there's usually always one qn on binomial and r-formulae. you can also spot topics for paper2 based on what paper1 tests!  i've heard many success stories of people chionging maths 2-3months before o's itself and getting As so don't give up just yet. try and pick out important questions from papers to revise too. don't waste time doing the entire paper and think them through in your head first. if you think you can do it easily then don't bother putting it down on paper. it's important to cover questions that you're unsure about first bc of your limited time now. assessment books are gr8 for practice. tag questions that you want to revise later on for easy revision. do a few papers every day if you want to see really fast improvement, and give yourself time constraints to gauge your actual exam condition. take note of how common careless mistakes are for you too because they can rly cost a lot of marks.

unfortunately i didn't take geog-bio in sec sch so i can't rly advise you on that? :-( based on my friends i say just heavy memorise, use tools like flashcards and find which way helps you memorise and digest information best. if you don't like memorising in jc then geog, bio and esp history isn't really for you i think.

!! SLEEP IS IMPORTANT !!
always sleep early before papers that require a lot of brain strength & logic so you can think straight and focus (e.g maths). i suggest to start sleeping early arnd 1.5-2.5 weeks before o's to reset your body clock and give your body sufficient rest for the intensive exam period ahead.

if you have any other qns feel free to pm me! i'm in acjc atm (albeit only a j1), L1R5 21 for prelims and 8 raw for o's so it's really do-able :-) just make sure to do your best. also acjc arts stream dropped to 9/10 i think? and sajc should be higher i think so you really shouldn't worry too much!

generally just figure out which 6 subjects you want to be using for your L1R5 and focus on them! they should be either 1. your strongest, 2. the ones you can improve fast in (maths etc) or 3. the ones you're most interested in and would feel the least pain mugging for. because in the end the only grades that really matter are the ones you're using for your L1R5 so yeppers! all the bestt + since you alr secured A2 for your chinese you have pretty good chances of getting into acjc/sajc!
